subject: english
title: Connectors
description: although, despite, however, therefore — joining ideas without losing the grammar.

content.title: Why they matter
content.body: Connectors signal the relationship between two ideas: contrast, cause, result, addition. Choosing the right one is half the work; the other half is knowing what has to follow it grammatically.

content.title: The pattern that trips people up
content.body: although + clause (subject + verb). despite / in spite of + noun or -ing. However starts a new sentence and takes a comma. Get these three right and your writing immediately reads as C1.

content.title: Good practice
content.body: "Despite of" does not exist. It is either despite or in spite of — never a blend of the two.

exercises.question: Vocabulary
exercises.explanation: A connector introducing contrast: Although it was late, she kept studying.

exercises.question: Complete the sentence.
exercises.sentence: ___ the delay, the release went out on time.

answers.text: However
Although
Despite
Because

exercises.explanation: What follows is a noun phrase, so despite is correct. Although would need a full clause: Although it was delayed, ...

exercises.question: Which sentence uses however correctly?

answers.text: However the tests passed, the build failed.
The tests passed. However, the build failed.
The tests passed however the build failed.
The tests passed, however failed the build.

exercises.explanation: However is an adverb, not a conjunction: it opens a new sentence (or follows a semicolon) and takes a comma.

exercises.question: Translate the sentence.
exercises.sentence: The API was down, therefore the tests failed.

answers.text: API nie działało, dlatego testy się wywaliły.
API nie działało, chociaż testy się wywaliły.
API nie działało, mimo że testy przeszły.
API nie działało, o ile testy się wywaliły.

exercises.explanation: therefore marks a result, so Polish uses dlatego / w związku z tym.

exercises.question: "Despite of the rain, we went out" is correct.
exercises.explanation: It is despite the rain or in spite of the rain. "Despite of" mixes the two forms.

exercises.question: What has to follow "although"?

answers.text: A clause with its own subject and verb
A noun phrase
Nothing — it can end a sentence
An -ing form

exercises.explanation: Although is a conjunction and joins two clauses. despite and in spite of are prepositions and take a noun or -ing.

exercises.question: Complete the sentence expressing purpose.
exercises.sentence: We added retries ___ to make the suite less flaky.

answers.text: in order
so that
because
for

exercises.explanation: in order to + infinitive expresses purpose. so that would need a full clause: so that the suite is less flaky.

exercises.question: What does whereas signal?

answers.text: An example
A cause
A direct contrast between two facts
A time sequence

exercises.explanation: Unit tests are fast, whereas end-to-end tests are slow. It contrasts two things without suggesting either is unexpected.

exercises.question: Vocabulary
exercises.explanation: Same job as however, one register higher. Common in written reports, rare in speech.

exercises.question: Complete the sentence.
exercises.sentence: The release slipped ___ a failing integration test.

answers.text: because
due to
therefore
although

exercises.explanation: due to and because of take a noun phrase; because takes a full clause: because an integration test failed.

exercises.question: Which sentence adds information correctly?

answers.text: In addition of the report, we sent the metrics.
In addition the report, we sent the metrics.
In addition to the report, we sent the metrics.
In addition with the report, we sent the metrics.

exercises.explanation: in addition to + noun. On its own, "In addition," opens a sentence with a comma.

exercises.question: Translate the sentence.

answers.text: As a result, we had to roll back the release.
In result, we had to roll back the release.
As result we had to roll back the release.
On the result, we had to roll back the release.

exercises.explanation: The fixed phrase is "as a result", with the article, followed by a comma when it opens the sentence.

exercises.question: Beginning a sentence with "And" or "But" is a grammatical error.
exercises.explanation: It is a style preference, not a rule, and it is common in good writing. In a formal report, However or In addition simply reads better.

exercises.question: What separates moreover from also?

answers.text: Register — moreover is formal and adds a stronger point; also is neutral and mid-sentence
Moreover can only be used in questions
Also cannot begin a sentence
They are interchangeable in every context

exercises.explanation: Moreover signals that what follows strengthens the argument. Overusing it in speech sounds stilted.

exercises.question: Vocabulary
exercises.back: niezależnie od — followed by a noun, never by that
exercises.explanation: Regardless of the result, we ship on Friday. "Irregardless" is not a word in standard English.
